newsitem.title: INDIA: Cargo ship sinks in Calcutta, crew rescued.
newsitem.headline: Cargo ship sinks in Calcutta, crew rescued.

text.p: Panama-flag cargo ship M.V. Green Opal, carrying 70,000 tonnes of steel, sank in a river in the eastern city of Calcutta on Thursday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
All the vessel's crew were rescued, it said.
K.K. Kalia, a senior police official, told Reuters in Calcutta that the ship sank in the Hooghly river about 40 km (25 miles) from Calcutta, on its way to Hong Kong.

PTI quoted Calcutta Port Trust officials as saying the captain, the chief officer and the second officer were Korean and the remaining crew members were Philippine. It said all 20 crew members had been saved.
"We know some crew members were rescued but details are awaited," Kalia said.
PTI said the ship sank after hitting a barge.
Naval helicopters and coast guard ships were pressed into the search for 20 missing crew members, a defence spokesman told Reuters.
"We rescued 13 people, of whom four died soon after being taken to hospital," the spokesman said. "We're looking for about 20 more people." There was a woman among the dead, he added.
"The last port of call of the ship was Arruways in the United Arab Emirates," the federal government said in a statement. "It was bringing sulphur to Bombay."
Officials of the firm that owns the vessel, Arcadia Shipping Pvt. Ltd, were not immediately available for comment.
